item.title: Jonathan Greenard feels "close," but Eagles' plan for Sunday remains unknown
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Linebacker Jonathan Greenard has been practicing for the Eagles this week, but it remains unclear whether he'll be on the field against the Commanders on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Linebacker Jonathan Greenard has been practicing for the Eagles this week, but it remains unclear whether he'll be on the field against the Commanders on Sunday.

Greenard did not practice at all this summer due to a pectoral injury and has been listed as limited on the first two injury reports of the week. Friday will bring another practice and the issuing of injury designations that could shed more light on whether the offseason acquisition will be part of the Week 1 plan.

“They haven’t told me anything,” Greenard said Thursday, via Reuben Frank of NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com. “I just know I've been getting right, going through the motions of just trying to get back into the swing of things before I get fully thrown out there. But it's something every day. So I just listen to them. I trust their judgment. I'm literally just trying to work day by day. Like, I literally am out there every second trying to just show what I can do. And that's tough for them, but I feel pretty solid. . . . It’s not for me to decide. I feel good, though. I will say I feel I'm in a good spot. I know that I'm working every day to continue to try to get this thing stronger. We're close. I know that.”

Greenard will likely play a reduced number of snaps if he is active against Washington, but the Eagles will take whatever they can get if Greenard is ready to start helping the team's pass rush.

item.title: Packers DC Jonathan Gannon: Kyler Murray can wreck games if you're not coordinated
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jonathan Gannon-Kyler Murray partnership in Arizona ended with both men moving on after the 2025 season, but they'll be back together for the first game of their new starts.
item.content:encoded:
The Jonathan Gannon-Kyler Murray partnership in Arizona ended with both men moving on after the 2025 season, but they'll be back together for the first game of their new starts.

Gannon is now the Packers' defensive coordinator, which means he'll be charged with slowing Murray down in his debut as the Vikings' starting quarterback. In a press conference this week, Gannon said that his experience coaching Murray left him aware of exactly what the defense has to be on guard for on Sunday.

"Really good player," Gannon said, via WLUK. "He's in a really good offense with some elite players. Obviously I've got nothing but love and respect for K-1. He's competitive, he's smart, he can make all the throws and he can beat you with his legs. So a bigtime challenge. As I know firsthand what this guy can do with his legs and he can train wreck the game real fast if you're not coordinated the right way. We gotta contain him. We gotta be ready to plaster at all times 'cause he has just kind of a way of getting out that pocket and extending plays. And then when he's out that pocket is when I think he's most dangerous."

Murray was shut down after hurting his foot early in the 2025 season and that decision was tied to contractual matters as the Cardinals wanted to avoid being on the hook for any of his 2027 money. That didn't help Gannon keep his job and shutting down his former quarterback would be the best way to start his new gig on the right foot.

item.title: Matthew Stafford rarely succeeds on quarterback sneaks, but Rams tried one anyway
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: With the Rams facing fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line on Thursday night, Matthew Stafford attempted a quarterback sneak.
item.content:encoded:
With the Rams facing fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line on Thursday night, Matthew Stafford attempted a quarterback sneak. It did not go well: Stafford took the snap and fell into the line, going nowhere and ending what had been an excellent drive just short of the goal line.

That raised an obvious question: Why was a quarterback sneak the play call? Stafford isn't Jalen Hurts or Josh Allen. He's a 38-year-old who attempted two quarterback sneaks last year and failed on both of them, and who didn't gain as much as a single rushing first down in 17 regular-season games last year.

Rams coach Sean McVay said after the game that he viewed failing to score at the end of that 12-play, 72-yard drive as the moment the wind went out of the Rams' sails.

"We go right down the field and then we don't get in on the QB sneak, and things got out of hand from there," McVay said.

Given that, McVay needs to look in the mirror at his own play-calling decision. Stafford confirmed that the sneak was a called play and not something he did on his own.

"I've just got to find a way to get in," Stafford said.

If McVay wanted to sneak it in from the 1-yard line, it would have made more sense for the Rams to snap the ball to a tight end or running back, which many teams with aging or immobile quarterbacks do. Or McVay simply could have called another short-yardage play. McVay's decision to go for it on fourth-and-goal was a good one, but the play call was a bad one.

item.title: Fred Warner felt the Rams "withered away" as game went on
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Rams took a 7-3 lead over the 49ers on the first play of the second quarter on Thursday night, but it was not a sign that things were going to go their way for the rest of their time in Melbourne, Australia.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams took a 7-3 lead over the 49ers on the first play of the second quarter on Thursday night, but it was not a sign that things were going to go their way for the rest of their time in Melbourne, Australia.

A Demarcus Robinson touchdown catch put the 49ers up 10-7 at halftime and the 49ers would score 17 more points in the second half while shutting out the Rams. The biggest defensive play of that effort came when the Niners stoned the Rams on four goal-to-go plays in the third quarter, including a Matthew Stafford sneak on fourth down that went nowhere.

Linebacker Fred Warner was at the point of attack on that play and many others over the course of the 27-7 win. He finished his first game back from a serious ankle injury with 11 tackles and a forced fumble in the fourth quarter. After it was over, he pointed to the different approaches the two teams took in going to Australia — the 49ers were there for a week, the Rams got there the day before — in helping to fuel the way things played out.

“I think it was definitely a matter of us feeling like we got stronger as the game went on," Warner said in a postgame press conference. "The opposing team, it felt like they kinda withered away. . . . Our plan was great. Coming out here early, all the resources they gave us to be successful for today is what gave us a chance to win this game."

The second half of the travel question is the impact it will have on the two teams once they are back home. Time will tell how that plays out, but having Warner back in the middle of the defense should only help their chances of keeping things rolling.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: I love calling plays for Mike Evans
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Mike Evans built his career with the Buccaneers on being the guy quarterbacks looked to on third down and in the red zone, and it didn't take long for him to take on the same role with the 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Evans built his career with the Buccaneers on being the guy quarterbacks looked to on third down and in the red zone, and it didn't take long for him to take on the same role with the 49ers.

Evans converted three third downs on the team's opening drive to set up a field goal and the wideout extended the 49ers' lead to 17-7 by catching a fade from Brock Purdy for a touchdown in the third quarter. Evans finished the 27-7 win with six catches for 49 yards and head coach Kyle Shanahan said at his postgame press conference that he's already realized that "I love calling plays for Mike."

Shanahan also noted that Evans missed time this summer and that his connection with Purdy should only get stronger.

"We've watched Mike do that for his whole career," Shanahan said. "I've just never been on the team with him. I mean, he did that to us a ton when I was in Atlanta. Mike is as good as any receiver who's played down there. Hadn't got to work on it as much as we would like during training camp. It was something that we told them early on that we wanted them doing when they were in Tennessee working together [this offseason]. They were working on the side a little bit this week, and I said I want to give them more opportunities to get better at it, but they didn't need it today. They looked pretty good at it."

The 49ers saw another wideout go down with injury during the win and any absence for De'Zhaun Stribling will make Evans even more important to the offensive plans that Shanahan draws up in the weeks to come.

item.title: Sean McVay: "This will define us only if we allow it to"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Something happened on the road to a perfect season for the Rams.
item.content:encoded:
Something happened on the road to a perfect season for the Rams. The road took them to Australia, where they got their butts kicked, 27-7, by the division rival they hand-picked to face there.

After the loss to the 49ers, Rams coach Sean McVay accepted the outcome — but he won't regard it as the start of a trend.

"This will define us only if we allow it to," McVay told reporters. "And today was one of those days."

McVay took the blame for the loss.

"I always look inside-out," he said. "I didn't do [a] good enough job getting us ready to go. There were some opportunities where maybe the game could have flipped, but they deserved the win. They were ready to go. And we'll look at it. We'll see where we can improve, and be better moving forward.

"But this is a good humbling day. This is what can sometimes happen in sports. I love this locker room and, you know, the first thing that I'm gonna look at is myself, and I have to do a better job for a group collectively, with our coaches, with our players, and we'll look at this film, and we'll get back to work because, clearly, that's obviously what we've got to do, and sometimes sports can humble you, and today was one of those days."

The travel decision will loom over the showing, and McVay mentioned it.

"I make no excuses and, you know, whether you want to say it's about travel, whatever, we just weren't good enough in that window," McVay said. "I didn't coach good enough, and we'll look at it and we'll move forward, and that's where we're at right now. But it was a great atmosphere. Give credit to the 49ers. They deserve it, and we're 0-1, and we'll move forward."

Sixteen games remain. The only thing we know at this point is that the 49ers can't be worse than 1-16, and the Rams can't be better than 16-1. Still, the Week 14 rematch will loom over L.A. Another loss to the 49ers means a sweep, which becomes a de facto three-game hole in the standings vs. San Francisco.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: Win or lose, everyone would make a big deal about our travel schedules
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The 49ers and Rams took opposite approaches to the longest road trip in NFL history: The 49ers arrived in Australia a full week early to give themselves time to acclimate.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers and Rams took opposite approaches to the longest road trip in NFL history: The 49ers arrived in Australia a full week early to give themselves time to acclimate. The Rams arrived in Australia the day before in an attempt not to acclimate, and simply to act as if they were still at home. So does the 49ers' 27-7 win vindicate their approach?

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan downplayed that when asked if the 49ers' travel plan worked.

"I mean, the game worked," Shanahan said. "Win or lose, I knew everyone was going to make a big deal about that, for either team. You never know how much that factors into it, you just try to do the best to prepare for three and a half hours. I liked how we prepared, but more importantly I liked how we played."

Shanahan said he hopes to visit Australia as a tourist some day but didn't focus on anything but football for this trip.

"I'd like to come back when I'm not working, enjoy it a little more," Shanahan said. "It's tough to have fun when you're working all week."

Asked if he'd like to return to Australia for another game, Shanahan said he'd always prefer to avoid long road trips.

"To play? I'd like 17 home games in San Francisco," Shanahan said. "Nothing against Australia, I just don't like to travel."

item.title: Myles Garrett: "This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Garrett said he needs to get healthy after missing most of training camp with a knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
Myles Garrett didn't have a single tackle, sack or pressure in his much-hyped debut for the Rams on Thursday night, and afterward he said the 27-7 loss to the 49ers was as bad a game as he's ever played.

"This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there," Garrett said. "I've got to be better. I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before."

Garrett, who didn't play in the preseason and barely practiced in training camp because of a knee injury, said his primary focus now is "getting healthy."

"That's the main thing," Garrett said. "When I was out there I was a little more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and it showed. I wasn't what I needed to be for my team."

Garrett said he didn't think the long trip to Australia or the Rams' decision to arrive the day before the game had anything to do with it.

"I wasn't the player I wanted to be, I didn't feel like I was the player I've been before when I stepped onto that field. I've got to do what I can to get back to that," Garrett said.

Garrett, the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year whose trade to the Rams was the NFL's most talked-about offseason move, was a total non-factor against the 49ers. The Rams have to hope that was the worst version of him they'll see.

item.title: 49ers tight end Jake Tonges suffers MCL injury, Kyle Shanahan says "it wasn't good"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: 49ers tight end Jake Tonges left Thursday night's win over the Rams with a knee injury, and coach Kyle Shanahan offered an ominous update after the game.
item.content:encoded:
49ers tight end Jake Tonges left Thursday night's win over the Rams with a knee injury, and coach Kyle Shanahan offered an ominous update after the game.

"It wasn't good. It's not an ACL, it's the MCL, I believe, but there's some issues with it that we've got to see how it is. There's a little more information to it, but we don't know yet," Shanahan said.

The 49ers likely won't know the full extent of Tonges' injury until they're back from Australia and can give him a full battery of tests, but Shanahan's tone suggested that the medical staff thinks Tonges will miss significant time.

The 27-year-old Tonges has been with the 49ers since 2023. He spent his first year in San Francisco on the practice squad and played mostly special teams in 2024, but he saw a much bigger role on offense in 2025 because of injuries to George Kittle. Last year Tonges caught 34 passes for 293 yards and five touchdowns, and this offseason he signed a two-year, $8 million contract.

item.title: 49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling's Achilles is intact, to undergo MRI on ankle
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The way 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suddenly ended his route and started limping on one leg had everyone thinking the worst.
item.content:encoded:
The way 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suddenly ended his route and started limping on one leg had everyone thinking the worst.

Stribling has an injured left ankle, coach Kyle Shanahan said after the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams, but the rookie's Achilles is intact.

Stribling will undergo further medical testing to determine the severity of the injury.

He injured his ankle early in the game and was questionable to return, but after running up and down the sideline, Stribling did return.

With 7:16 remaining in the first half, though, Stribling pulled up while running a route. He could not put any weight on his left leg and needed help to get to the sideline medical tent. Eventually, Stribling was carted to the X-ray room.

The 49ers quickly ruled him out.

He had no catches.

item.title: Cowboys agree to terms with WR Ryan Flournoy on one-year extension
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys have agreed to terms with wide receiver Ryan Flournoy on a one-year contract extension, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys have agreed to terms with wide receiver Ryan Flournoy on a one-year contract extension, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.

The deal is worth up to $6 million.

Flournoy, 26, was entering the final year of his deal, which will pay him $1.075 million in 2026. He would have become a restricted free agent in 2027.

After being waived out of training camp, Flournoy became the team's third wide receiver last season. He caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns, earning a promotion to the active roster from the practice squad early in the season.

The Cowboys drafted him in the sixth round in 2024, and he played 156 offensive snaps and 140 on special teams in 11 games as a rookie.

The team's leading receiver from last season, George Pickens, is playing under the one-year franchise tag and is scheduled to become a free agent in March.

item.title: The 49ers-Rams travel question won't be fully resolved until Week 2, or beyond
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Based on Thursday night's smothering down under by the 49ers against the Rams, it appears that San Francisco's early-arrival approach worked better than the Rams' strategy of barnstorming.
item.content:encoded:
Based on Thursday night's smothering down under by the 49ers against the Rams, it appears that San Francisco's early-arrival approach worked better than the Rams' strategy of barnstorming.

But Week 1 is just part of the equation. The Rams were surely thinking about the recovery from the long trip, with the goal of being ready for the next game, against the Giants to cap Week 2.

And it doesn't get easy after that. The Rams travel to Denver for a Sunday night game before playing in Philadelphia the next Sunday afternoon. After that, it's another Monday night game — against the Bills.

The 49ers will have to fly home after fully acclimating to Australia and re-acclimating to America. The Dolphins come to town in Week 2, followed by visits from the Cardinals and Broncos. In Week 5, the 49ers make their annual visit to the Seahawks.

In many respects, Thursday night's game is only the beginning. Where both teams go from here after going home will show plenty.

item.title: Brock Purdy, 49ers dominate Rams 27-7 in Australia
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The 49ers quarterback outplayed Matthew Stafford, completing 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and an interception.
item.content:encoded:
Much will be made of the travel arrangements for the 49ers and Rams, but Los Angeles better hope its lackluster performance is jet lag and nothing more.

The 49ers dominated the Rams from start to finish, winning 27-7 in Melbourne.

San Francisco spent the past week in Australia, while Los Angeles showed up 28 hours before kickoff and stayed on Pacific Time in its brief stay. The 49ers not only looked like the fresher team but the better team.

Mike Evans scored a touchdown in his 49ers' debut; Deebo Samuel scored a touchdown in his return; Nick Bosa, Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw showed what a difference they make to the team's defense; and Trent Williams confirmed he's the best left tackle in the game.

Brock Purdy outplayed the reigning NFL MVP, completing 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also ran for 29 yards on five carries.

Purdy's touchdowns covered 39 yards to Demarcus Robinson, 5 yards to Evans and 15 yards to Samuel. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards, with five of his catches converting third downs, and Samuel had six catches for 48 yards and a 45-yard kickoff return.

49ers kicker Eddy Piñeiro kicked field goals of 20 and 56 yards but hit the right upright and missed from 52 yards.

The 49ers had more yards (379 to 290), more first downs (23 to 15), more plays (64 to 57), fewer turnovers (one to two), fewer penalties (two to four) and a better third-down percentage (7-of-12 to 2-of-9).

Matthew Stafford threw an interception, had a 61.2 passer rating and failed on two fourth-down plays. In his previous 84 starts, Stafford had scored fewer than 10 points only once. He directed the Rams to only nine points in a 24-9 loss to the 49ers in 2022.

He was stopped short of the goal line by Warner and rookie Gracen Halton on a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-goal from the 1 with 3:46 remaining in the third quarter. Then, with 7:54 left, he threw incomplete on fourth-and-9 to end all hope of a comeback.

He finished 15-of-25 for 155 yards before turning it over to Stetson Bennett for mop-up duty with 3:29 left.

Kyren Williams scored the Rams' only touchdown on a 5-yard run, giving them their only lead at 7-3.

Puka Nacua caught five passes for 74 yards.

Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, did nothing in his Rams debut. He had no stats, spending much of his night going one-on-one with Williams, and appeared gassed in the fourth quarter.

Garrett did not practice much this summer due to knee swelling.

Warner totaled 11 tackles, a pass defensed and a forced fumble; Greenlaw had six tackles; and Bosa recorded four tackles, two for loss, and a quarterback hit.

item.title: "Excited" Kyler Murray is ready for his Vikings' debut
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The first pick in the 2019 draft is getting a fresh start on Sunday, with the team he grew up rooting for.
item.content:encoded:
The first pick in the 2019 draft is getting a fresh start on Sunday, with the team he grew up rooting for.

And Kyler Murray is ready for the moment.

"I'm excited," Murray told reporters on Thursday. "Out of my, I don't know how many years I played football, this has got to be right up there for the most anticipated. I can't tell you how excited and ready I am to just be on the field again. Like I said, I haven't played since October, so it's been a long time for me."

Will he be feeling any nerves in his debut as a Viking?

"Nerves? Honestly, I've been playing football my whole life," Murray said. "If I didn't have, you know, those anxious butterflies, those nerves, I feel like, you know, maybe I shouldn't be doing it anymore, but I do believe, you know, I'm excited. I'm excited, and, you know, I can't wait."

He'll also be a captain in his first season with the Vikings.

"It means a lot," Murray said. "It means the world, actually. I mean, for me to be here, a new guy, and the guys, you know, put their faith and trust in me. It's emotional, but like I said, it means a lot. I'm appreciative, and I take great pride and honor to wear that 'C' on my chest."

The Vikings get a big game right out of the gates, against the Packers at home. A win fueled by a strong performance from Murray will provide instant validation of the effort to sign him. A loss will lead to head scratching for a team that should be good enough, on paper, to get back to the postseason.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The 49ers have a big lead in the fourth quarter, having dominated the first three plus quarters.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have a big lead in the fourth quarter, having dominated the first three plus quarters. The Rams will need a big comeback for a season-opening win.

San Francisco leads 24-7 with 12:57 remaining.

The 49ers took control by stopping Matthew Stafford on a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-goal from the 1 with 3:46 remaining in the third quarter. Fred Warner and rookie Gracen Halton stopped the Rams quarterback short of the gaol line.

The play was upheld on replay.

The 49ers then drove 99 yards in 11 plays, with Deebo Samuel catching a 15-yard touchdown. It was Brock Purdy's third touchdown pass, following a 39-yarder to Demarcus Robinson and a 5-yarder to Mike Evans.

Purdy is 24-of-32 for 205 yards with an interception.

The 49ers have outgained the Rams 358 to 222.

On third-and-goal, Evans snatched the ball away from cornerback Jaylen Watson.

He has six catches for 49 yards and a touchdown, with five receptions coming on third down.

The seven-play, 51-yard touchdown drive was set up by Deebo Samuel's 45-yard kickoff return.

Purdy is now 20-of-28 for 157 yards with two touchdowns and an interception.

The 49ers have ruled out tight end Jake Tonges, who injured his knee late in the first half. They had already ruled out rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, with a left ankle injury.

item.title: 49ers lead Rams 10-7 at halftime in Australia
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The 49ers have outgained the Rams 208 to 137.
item.content:encoded:
Matthew Stafford hasn't looked like the MVP he was last year. Yet.

The Rams quarterback completed only 4 of 11 passes for 65 yards and an interception in the first half. Forty-one of those yards came on one throw to Puka Nacua that set up their only touchdown. Stafford's passer rating is 19.1.

The 49ers lead 10-7 at halftime, having outgained the Rams 208 to 137.

Brock Purdy went 17-of-25 for 141 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He threw a 39-yard strike to Demarcus Robinson for the 49ers' first touchdown of the season.

The 49ers settled for a chip-shot, 20-yard Eddy Piñeiro field goal on their first drive of the season, choosing not to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the Rams 2.

Mike Evans has five catches for 47 yards, and rookie Kaelon Black has run for 36 yards on seven carries. Christian McCaffrey has three carries for 17 yards and four catches for 20 yards.

Kyren Williams has the Rams' only touchdown, scoring on a 5-yard run after Nacua's long gainer to the 8. Williams has seven carries for 31 yards and Blake Corum six for 42.

49ers cornerback Renardo Green and Rams safety Quentin Lake each have an interception.

Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, had a quiet first half. He has no stats yet.

item.title: Reports: A.J. Brown is expected to miss at least four weeks
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown's ankle injury is expected to keep him out for an extended period of time.

According to multiple reports, an MRI on Thursday confirmed that Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain when he was injured during Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks. Those reports also say that Brown is expected to miss at least four weeks while he recovers from the injury. That time frame would make him a candidate for injured reserve, but there's no word on the team's plans at this point.

The Patriots face a run of 2025 playoff teams during the first weeks of Brown's expected absence. They host the Steelers in Week 2 before traveling to Jacksonville and Buffalo for their next two games.

Navigating that stretch without Brown will be tougher and it's not an ideal start to the wideout's tenure with the team. Drake Maye is coming off a three-interception fourth quarter in Seattle on Wednesday that also featured a crucial drop by Romeo Doubs. Doubs was the most prominent addition to the receiving corps for most of the offseason and the team will need him to thrive in a prominent role to get the offense on track without Brown.

item.title: Puka Nacua addresses "darkest times" in his life, fueled by "drowning" in alcohol
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Nacua opens up about time spent at a holistic rehab facility.
item.content:encoded:
Rams receiver Puka Nacua had a difficult and challenging offseason. In an interview with Elle Duncan of Netflix prior to L.A.'s season-opening game against the 49ers, Nacua called his experiences the "darkest times I've had in my life."

Nacua spent time in a holistic rehabilitation center. He was asked what he learned about himself.

"I think I learned that I'm very avoidant of conflict," Nacua said, "which is very interesting due to the football nature of — I would like to say, I play very physical, just avoidant of the things that I know were causing me stress."

Where did the stress come from?

"Just, I think, some of the change in lifestyle that came unto me, becoming a public figure, the stress of performing at a high level," Nacua said. "And then I recently became a father. My son is 10 months old, and navigating that co-parenting relationship with his mother, I would kind of isolate myself to feel, like, the weight of all the issues and things that I have was stuck on my shoulders and not being willing to ask for help. I was never one to share my fears, my worries. I was always finding different ways to escape, I guess, from that tension or that stress."

How did he deal with the stress?

"I think one, alcohol was definitely a thing for me. Just kind of drowning myself, so that the issues and the stress that I was feeling never had the opportunity to be addressed," Nacua said. "But right when I entered the rehabilitation center, I was able to have open and honest conversations."

There's still a potential price to be paid. A civil lawsuit is pending. As PFT reported earlier in the day, Nacua has commenced the process of fulfilling a diversion program in lieu of prosecution, which could prompt the NFL to take action sooner than later under the Personal Conduct Policy.

Perhaps most importantly, the off-field issues undoubtedly have delayed Nacua's reward for three seasons of high-level performance despite being a fifth-round pick. At a time when Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has a deal that averages more than $42 million per year in new money, Nacua enters the final year of his rookie deal, at only $5.767 million.

And he does indeed play with a very physical style. Which enhances the risk of injury. Which puts an even greater premium on shifting the injury risk to the Rams.

item.title: Roger Goodell: NFL will make announcement on Jed York when investigation is completed
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: An appearance by Commissioner Roger Goodell on the Netflix pregame show in advance of 49ers-Rams in Melbourne included a box-checking question about the no-contest plea by 49ers owner Jed York on a pair of misdemeanor charges arising from a prostitution-related arrest last month.
item.content:encoded:
An appearance by Commissioner Roger Goodell on the Netflix pregame show in advance of 49ers-Rams in Melbourne included a box-checking question about the no-contest plea by 49ers owner Jed York on a pair of misdemeanor charges arising from a prostitution-related arrest last month.

Goodell confirmed that the situation is being "looked at" under the Personal Conduct Policy.

"When we get it completed, we'll obviously make an announcement at that point in time," Goodell told Netflix host Elle Duncan.

Other areas of potential curiosity could have included, for instance, why it's taking so long, given that he resolved the case one day after the arrest? Likewise, it would have been fair to ask whether York will be held to a higher standard than would be applied to a player and, if so, how that may be reflected in the punishment.

It's a delicate balance, to be sure. The league surely prefers not to shine a spotlight on a source of embarrassment. And Netflix undoubtedly doesn't want to damage a burgeoning partnership.

Still, it happened. And the league doesn't hesitate to bang the drum on playing in the NFL being a privilege, not a right. When player behavior falls short of the league's standard, consequences are imposed — often swiftly and rarely equivocally.

And if there was any doubt about the other side of the coin, Netflix analyst Michael Irvin was not given an opportunity to repeat his "everybody’s paying for it" defense of York.

item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys have agreed to terms with backup tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford on a three-year extension, his agent, Mike McCartney, announced on social media.

Spann-Ford was scheduled to become a restricted free agent in 2027.

He was scheduled to make $966,666 this season.

The Cowboys signed the former Minnesota Golden Gopher as an undrafted free agent in 2024. He has played all 34 games since and supplanted Luke Schoonmaker, a second-round pick in 2023, as the team's No. 2 tight end.

He has made only 18 catches for 178 yards and a touchdown, but has played 25.5 percent of the team's offensive snaps over the past two seasons. He has also played 357 special teams snaps, becoming a core special teams player in 2025.

The team announced its inactives ahead of Thursday night's season opener against the Rams in Melbourne.

Quarterback Kurtis Rourke, cornerback Ephesians Prysock, running back Jordan James, wide receiver Jordan Watkins, linebacker Tatum Bethune and offensive tackle Enrique Cruz are the 49ers' inactives. Rourke is the emergency third quarterback.

49ers defensive tackle James Thompson (hamstring) was the only player on either team with an injury designation aside from Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald, who did not make the trip after recently coming out of retirement. Thompson is dressed for the game.

The 49ers placed defensive tackle Alfred Collins on season-ending injured reserve earlier. Collins tore a patellar tendon during practice earlier this week.

The team also elevated wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge and defensive end Ogbo Okoronkwo from the practice squad.

The Rams' inactives are wide receiver CJ Daniels, wide receiver Tutu Atwell, offensive lineman Bill Murray, tight end Max Klare and quarterback Ty Simpson. Simpson will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

That means Stetson Bennett is officially the backup quarterback to Matthew Stafford.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty expects to play in Sunday's season opener against the Dolphins.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty expects to play in Sunday's season opener against the Dolphins.

Jeanty said his ankle feels "really good" and he is "super excited" to get back on the field.

The second-year player practiced fully again Thursday, his second practice back since injuring his ankle Aug. 23 in a training camp practice.

"Any time away from the game, it’s tough," Jeanty said, via Ryan McFadden of ESPN. "But to get back out there, mainly with the guys, man, it felt good."

The injury appeared worse than it was when it happened, as Jeanty went down while attempting to catch a low pass from Kirk Cousins. But it wasn't, and Jeanty said he knew pretty quickly afterward that he would play against the Dolphins in Week 1.

"I knew it wasn't anything too bad, even though I couldn't put pressure on my foot," Jeanty said in speaking to reporters for the first time since his injury. "I figured it wouldn't be anything that's too long term."
